title: Kubernetes Namespaces Delete Events

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `kube:objects:namespaces` events with `verb=delete OR verb=DELETE` into `index=kube`. Confirm UC-4.9.8 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `kube:objects:namespaces` traffic without `verb=delete OR verb=DELETE`. Confirm UC-4.9.8 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=kube` sourcetype=`kube:objects:namespaces` collected via Splunk Connect for Kubernetes / cloud provider K8s audit inputs; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.9.8 — Kubernetes Namespaces Delete Events: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `kube:objects:namespaces` for search criteria `verb=delete OR verb=DELETE` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), unauthorized deletion detected by 'Kubernetes Namespaces Delete Events' can cause immediate outage, data loss, or ransomware impact before backups are validated. UC-4.9.8 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=kube sourcetype=kube:objects:namespaces.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=kube`.
• Install and configure Splunk Connect for Kubernetes / cloud provider K8s audit inputs with the modular input for `kube:objects:namespaces`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.9.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=kube sourcetype=kube:objects:namespaces.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:objects:namespaces" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:objects:namespaces" verb=delete OR verb=DELETE
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.8_kubernetes_namespaces_de_8"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `kube:objects:namespaces` in `index=kube` to detect kubernetes namespaces delete events. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_9_8_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Connect for Kubernetes / cloud provider K8s audit inputs and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of kubernetes namespaces delete events so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
